subject: Post-demo: model-eval artifacts & prompt sample request (next steps)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model-eval artifacts & prompt sample request (next steps)

Hi Samira — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can scope a short eval: 

Summary (2 bullets):
- Goal: Replace FinLytics’ current rule-based summarization for earnings-call highlights with a single LLM-powered pipeline that preserves factuality and protects PII.
- Success metrics: ROUGE/ROUGE-L improvements vs baseline + precision on entity redaction (no PHI/SSN leakage).

What we need from you to set up an eval environment:
1) ~200 representative customer prompts / queries (mix of short & long queries; include the most frequent 30 and 40 edge cases)
2) 10–15 gold examples for evaluation (input + expected summary/label)
3) any sensitive-fields redaction guidance or regexes you already apply (we can mirror these in the eval harness)
4) a contact for legal/procurement so we can share an SOW and security questionnaire

Ben and Irene — can you please add recommended model candidates and an initial benchmark plan inline?

We’ll: provision a temporary eval project, run 3 model families (open-llama/quantized, llama-3 variants, and a 8-bit gpt-like baseline), and share raw outputs + a short regression checklist focused on hallucination and entity leakage.

Deliverable timeline: we can start once we receive the artifacts (1–2 business days to stand up the eval infra, 3–5 business days to run a first pass).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a Drive link to a secure intake folder.

— Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Redaction guidance: we currently mask SSNs, credit-card numbers, and any 3rd-party personal identifiers per our internal policy. I’ll attach the current redaction policy.
- Legal/procurement: looping in procurement for SOW and an initial NDA/POC agreement.

I’m attaching a CSV with 40 sample prompts and a brief redaction doc. We’ll upload the rest to the Drive link you send.

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model-eval artifacts & prompt sample request (next steps)

Dylan / Irene — quick model recommendations based on FinLytics’ constraints (high factuality, regulatory sensitivity, US region):

1) Candidate A: Llama-3-13B-rl - good F1 on entity preservation in our internal BA bench; lower token cost than larger families.
2) Candidate B: Open-Quant-7B (8-bit) - very cost-effective for high-throughput; watch for occasional brevity errors on long transcripts.
3) Candidate C: Llama-70B-q4o (safeguarded) - highest quality baseline, use as an upper-bound for hallucination checks.

Benchmark plan (first pass):
- Run 500 transcript snippets through all candidates (short + long prompts)
- Measure: ROUGE-L, entity-precision (custom NER), hallucination score (LM hallucination classifier)
- Regression triggers: >3% drop in entity-precision OR any output that contains an unredacted numeric identifier matching SSN/CC pattern
I'll prepare the perf/cost estimates and add them to the Drive folder.

— Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Samira — I downloaded the 40-sample CSV (appreciate the quick turnaround). Attached below is a short intake checklist and redaction guidance we use for evaluations — please confirm we should apply FinLytics’ current regex blocks (SSN, CC) exactly as-is or whether we should transform/mask them before upload.

Intake checklist (short):
- File format: CSV (col: prompt_id, raw_query, normalized_query, context_meta)
- Volume: target 200–300 prompts; please flag the 30 highest-priority utterances (we’ll hard-prioritize these in the first run)
- Edge cases: copy/paste the worst-case long transcript snippets into a separate file so we can evaluate KV-cache/attention behavior
- PII redaction: either provide masked inputs (recommended) or provide raw inputs + redaction regexes (we’ll run our sanitizer)

Quality/regression note for FinLytics: we will run an automatic regression check against the 15 gold examples you provide. Any candidate that produces an output containing an unredacted numeric identifier matching SSN/CC patterns will be flagged and paused. We’ll also surface hallucination examples in the dashboard for manual triage.

Privacy & transfer: we’ll share a dedicated, access-controlled Drive folder (link below) and a short intake template. If procurement prefers an SFTP or an encrypted transfer method, confirm and we’ll accommodate.

Drive intake (temp): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-artifacts
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789/RDW-2027-00123

Next steps: Samira — can you either (A) upload the remaining prompts into the Drive folder, masked per your policy, or (B) share raw files + the redaction regexes by EOB Monday? We’ll plan the first eval run once we have the 200 prompts.

— Dylan
